content:
After releasing the seventh developer builds of iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and Apple's other upcoming software updates, Apple is now beginning to push out the corresponding public beta versions to public beta testers. Here are the details.

Apple releases new public beta versions

Apple earlier today released:

  • iOS 27 developer build 7 (build number: 24A5424a)
  • iPadOS 27 developer build 7 (build number: 24A5424a)
  • macOS 27 Golden Gate developer build 7 (build number: 26A5421a)
  • tvOS 27 developer build 7 (build number: 24J5358a)
  • visionOS 27 developer build 7 (build number: 24M5359a)
  • watchOS 27 developer build 7 (build number: 24R5358a)

Apple is now pushing out the corresponding builds to public beta testers, marking the fifth public beta release of this cycle. Apple has so far released new public beta versions of iOS 27, tvOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and HomePod 27.

Today's release does not include any particularly notable new features, as Apple is now primarily focused on bug fixes and stability improvements ahead of the official launch, which is expected in a few weeks.

In addition, Apple has also released the second public beta RC of macOS Sequoia 15.8 (24H20), following the corresponding developer RC released earlier this morning. The second RC of macOS Tahoe 26.7 (25G224) is expected to be released soon. It became available for download at 7:42 PM Eastern Time.

Across all of today's releases, the public beta build numbers match those of the developer builds.

Sign up for the Apple Beta Program

To enrol your device in the public beta program, visit https://beta.apple.com and follow the steps for each respective device. Here's how to install the public beta version on your iPhone:

  • Go to the Apple Beta Software Program website and choose to enrol or sign in.
  • Sign in with the same Apple Account you use on your iPhone, then accept the program terms and enrol your account.
  • Open Settings on your iPhone.
  • Go to General > Software Update > Beta Updates.
  • Select "iOS 27 Public Beta".
  • Return to the Software Update page, and when the public beta version appears, tap "Update Now".

Apple recommends installing Beta software on a secondary device. If you use your primary iPhone, be sure to make a recent backup first.

Have you spotted any new features in today's public beta? Let us know in the comments.
